text: What I cannot create, I do not understand.
author: Richard P. Feynman
source: Final blackboard at Caltech (1988)

text: We can only see a short distance ahead, but we can see plenty there that needs to be done.
author: Alan M. Turing
source: Computing Machinery and Intelligence (1950)

text: We may say most aptly that the Analytical Engine weaves algebraical patterns just as the Jacquard-loom weaves flowers and leaves.
author: Ada Lovelace
source: Notes on the Analytical Engine (1843)

text: If I have seen further it is by standing on the shoulders of Giants.
author: Isaac Newton
source: Letter to Robert Hooke (1675)

text: Science and everyday life cannot and should not be separated.
author: Rosalind Franklin
source: Letter to Ellis Franklin (1940), quoted by Brenda Maddox

text: Nothing in life is to be feared, it is only to be understood.
author: Marie Curie
source: Quoted by the Nobel Foundation, Annual Review 2024

text: The universe is not only stranger than we suppose, but stranger than we can suppose.
author: J. B. S. Haldane
source: Possible Worlds and Other Essays (1927)

text: Ignorance more frequently begets confidence than does knowledge.
author: Charles Darwin
source: The Descent of Man (1871)

text: Coffee is not a research method, but it has attended a suspicious number of discoveries.
author: Anonymous
source: Creative field note

text: Every well-organized drawer is a local victory over entropy and a temporary one.
author: ARIEL RESEARCH SYSTEM
source: Creative field note

text: The first principle is that you must not fool yourself—and you are the easiest person to fool.
author: Richard P. Feynman
source: Cargo Cult Science, Caltech commencement address (1974)

text: Research your own experience. Absorb what is useful, reject what is useless, add what is essentially your own.
author: Bruce Lee
source: Research Your Own Experience, Bruce Lee official archive

text: The important thing is not to stop questioning. Curiosity has its own reason for existing.
author: Albert Einstein
source: Statement to William Miller, LIFE (2 May 1955)

text: The scientist must not merely find and communicate new truth, but teach and bring an honest, intelligible account of knowledge to all who try to learn.
author: J. Robert Oppenheimer
source: Uncommon Sense (ed. 2013)

text: Philosophy is written in this grand book, the universe, which stands continually open to our gaze.
author: Galileo Galilei
source: The Assayer (1623), translated by Stillman Drake

text: The progressive development of man is vitally dependent on invention.
author: Nikola Tesla
source: My Inventions (1919), chapter 1

text: He who loves practice without theory is like the sailor who boards ship without a rudder and compass and never knows where he may cast.
author: Leonardo da Vinci
source: The Notebooks of Leonardo da Vinci, translated by Edward MacCurdy

text: It is not enough to have a good mind. The main thing is to use it well.
author: René Descartes
source: Discourse on the Method, part I (1637)

text: The saddest aspect of life right now is that science gathers knowledge faster than society gathers wisdom.
author: Isaac Asimov
source: The Roving Mind, Creationism and the Schools (1983)

text: We are a way for the cosmos to know itself.
author: Carl Sagan
source: Cosmos: A Personal Voyage (1980)

text: Music is a secret exercise of arithmetic where the mind is unaware that it is counting.
author: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz
source: Letter to Christian Goldbach (17 April 1712)

text: Give me a place to stand, and I shall move the world.
author: Archimedes
source: Attributed by Pappus of Alexandria, Collection, book VIII

text: I have discovered a truly marvelous proof of this, which this margin is too narrow to contain.
author: Pierre de Fermat
source: Marginal note in Diophantus's Arithmetica (c. 1637)

text: Thoughts without content are empty, intuitions without concepts are blind.
author: Immanuel Kant
source: Critique of Pure Reason, A51/B75

text: He who has a why to live for can bear with almost any how.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche
source: Twilight of the Idols, Maxims and Arrows, §12 (1888)

text: The universe is transformation: life is opinion.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations, book IV, §3, translated by George Long

text: Ah! terrible is knowledge to the man whom knowledge profits not.
author: Sophocles
source: Oedipus Tyrannus, translated by Lewis Campbell

text: All men by nature desire to know.
author: Aristotle
source: Metaphysics, book I, 980a21

text: We are not born for ourselves alone, but our country claims a share of our being, and our friends a share.
author: Marcus Tullius Cicero
source: De Officiis, book I, §22 (after Plato)

text: We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
author: Seneca
source: Moral Letters to Lucilius, letter 13, §4, translated by R. M. Gummere

text: The study of philosophy is not that we may know what men have thought, but what the truth of things is.
author: Thomas Aquinas
source: Commentary on Aristotle's De Caelo, book I, lecture 22

text: A wise man, therefore, proportions his belief to the evidence.
author: David Hume
source: An Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding, section X (1748)

text: The owl of Minerva spreads its wings only with the falling of the dusk.
author: G. W. F. Hegel
source: Elements of the Philosophy of Right, preface (1820)

text: If you assume that there is an instinct for freedom, that there are opportunities to change things, then there is a possibility that you can contribute to making a better world.
author: Noam Chomsky
source: Latin America: From Colonization to Globalization (1999)

text: The highest activity a human being can attain is learning for understanding, because to understand is to be free.
author: Baruch Spinoza
source: Modern paraphrase inspired by Ethics

text: The mind's highest good is the knowledge of God, and the mind's highest virtue is to know God.
author: Baruch Spinoza
source: Ethics, part IV, proposition 28
